Complete 0/1 Knapsack Template:
def knapsack(weights, values, capacity):
n = len(weights)
{{c1::dp = [0] * (capacity + 1)}}
{{c2::for i in range(n):}}
{{c3::for w in range(capacity, weights[i] - 1, -1):}} # Reverse!
{{c4::dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - weights[i]] + values[i])}}
return dp[capacity]

Complete Unbounded Knapsack Template:
def unboundedKnapsack(weights, values, capacity):
{{c1::dp = [0] * (capacity + 1)}}
{{c2::for w in range(1, capacity + 1):}}
for i in range(len(weights)):
{{c3::if weights[i] <= w:}}
{{c4::dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - weights[i]] + values[i])}}
return dp[capacity]

Front: 0/1 Knapsack key insight: Why iterate capacity in reverse?
Back: Prevents using same item multiple times. Each item used at most once.

Front: Unbounded Knapsack key insight: Why iterate capacity forward?
Back: Allows using same item multiple times. dp[w-weight] may already include current item.

Front: DP space optimization key insight: When can you use O(1) space?
Back: When current state only depends on previous 1-2 states (like Fibonacci).

Front: LIS binary search key insight: What does tails array represent?
Back: tails[i] = smallest tail element for LIS of length i+1. Enables binary search.

Front: DP edge case: empty input?
Back: Usually return 0 or handle specially at start
